Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

claim verb

say that something is so

also assert, allege, claim that, he claims

classical

Caes. BG 1.39.1: ingentī magnitūdine corporum Germānōs … esse praedicābant
Traupman 147, 291: Praedicat sē reī pūblicae prōfutūrum esse

praedicō, praedicāre, praedicāvī, praedicātum

verb, first conjugation; with an accusative and infinitive

claim, declare (openly)

Of saying out loud, to all and sundry, that something is so; ut praedicās, “as you claim” (Cic. Cat. 1.23, in Lewis & Short). Not praedīcō, praedīcere, foretell.

Other words

  • dictitō, dictitāre, dictitāvī, dictitātum — keep saying, claim (often falsely)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 743: quem semper tē esse dictitāstī; Caes. BC 3.22.3 (Lewis & Short): ut dictitābat

    Lewis & Short: “to declare, maintain, assert repeatedly”; Caesar’s ut dictitābat, “as he claimed”, gives a pretext.

  • contendō, contendere, contendī, contentum — maintain, insist (that)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Arch. 15: atque īdem ego hoc contendō

    With an accusative and infinitive: to argue a point hard.

  • affirmō, affirmāre, affirmāvī, affirmātum — assert, state as certain

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 2.8: nihil ut adfirmem, quaeram omnia

    Also spelled adfirmō.

Examples

  • Quid? nōn, obsecrō, es quem semper tē esse dictitāstī?

    What? Aren’t you, if you please, the man you always claimed to be?Ter. Ph. 742b–743

See also claim, say, statement.
